correctness.rationale: The lifting step follows by binomial expansion. In the coefficient argument, \(S=(p-1)d+m\) is not divisible by \(p\), every multinomial coefficient at degree \(S\) is divisible by \(p\), and the only term not carrying a coefficient divisible by \(p^n\) contributes \(p b_m\) modulo \(p^{n+1}\), a contradiction. The family \(P(x)=(1+x)^{p^n}\) is \(n\)-good by repeated lifting and has \(x\)-coefficient exactly \(p^n\), proving sharpness.
